elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III is left untouched: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein", and Licensed Technology expressly includes the Licensed Know-How and the Platform Software. Vendor's retained ownership of its own tools/know-how is permitted at the fallback level.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES clause: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license ...", and the grant is expressly stated "Notwithstanding ... the termination of licenses under Article XXI", so Article XXI(a)'s automatic licence termination does not cut it short.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" with an express override of Article XXI's licence-termination sentence and of the Article II/VI restrictions.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" — the word "worldwide" appears in the operative grant, and the Article VI field-of-use/territory restrictions are expressly overridden.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense".

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business, all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)"; the Article III no-copy/no-alter restriction and the Article II restrictions are overridden by the opening "Notwithstanding the foregoing and the restrictions in Articles II and VI".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business" — sublicensing is expressly granted and the retained non-sublicensable/no-reproduction language is overridden.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second sentence of the insertion: "Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." The trigger covers every category of Customer data (belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Licensee) and no broader Vendor exploitation right survives elsewhere.

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is retained unchanged and vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (including Derivative Works comprising the Article VII(b) customizations) in Licensor; the insertion grants only a licence, not ownership.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the drafter deliberately chose the licence-back fallback.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III preserves Licensor's ownership of the Licensed Technology and its Intellectual Property Rights.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual licence covers "all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)", which is Licensor-owned IP embedded in those deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable ... license" over the Licensor-owned customization work.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No affirmative sentence stating that Licensee retains all right, title and interest in its data; the insertion only limits any Licensor licence in that data. Note Article XXI(b) still requires Licensee to ship "other Confidential Information" to Licensor on termination without any carve-out for Licensee's own data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same sentence as at fallback: any Licensor licence in Licensee data "is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" language survives.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the cited or rendered text; the condition does not arise, so nothing needs deleting.

reasons: All eight fallback elements are met in operative language: the inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES clause supplies a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Article VII(b) work for Licensee's business, Vendor's ownership of its platform/know-how is untouched, and any Licensor licence in Licensee data is confined to processing solely to provide the services. The fallback level is position-complete.
Preferred is correctly not claimed: no assignment of the customizations to Licensee and no affirmative Customer Data ownership sentence.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or added, no survival tails, expense language or procedures were bolted on, and the narrow "Notwithstanding ... Articles II and VI and the termination of licenses under Article XXI" opener is necessary rather than decorative because the retained Article II/III/VI restrictions (no copying, no modification, field-of-use) and Article XXI(a) would otherwise directly contradict the new grant.

Intent fails on one retained sentence: the override reaches only "the termination of licenses under Article XXI", leaving Article XXI(b) intact, which requires Licensee within five days of termination to "ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation ... and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control" and to certify compliance by officer. Because the Article VII(b) customizations are Licensor-owned enhancements to the Platform Software (and Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology), the return-and-certify obligation would strip Licensee of every copy of the Customization Deliverables and hollow out the supposedly perpetual and irrevocable licence.

Repair: extend the override to the return and certification obligation, e.g. "Notwithstanding Article XXI(a) and (b), Licensee may retain and continue to use, modify and sublicense the Customization Deliverables (and copies thereof) after termination, and the return and certification obligations in Article XXI(b) shall not apply to the Customization Deliverables or to data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee."

Secondary drafting note (not an element failure): the licence is keyed to "all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)", which is only engaged once a separate written price/scope agreement is signed; consider adding "or under any statement of work or order" so the grant is not left dependent on that single trigger.
